slides.0.title: Terroir in depth
slides.0.subtitle: Comparing soils, altitude and sea wind
slides.1.title: Four factors for comparing regions
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Soil
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Decomposed granite on Stellenbosch slopes; Malmesbury shale in the Swartland interior; Bokkeveld shale (25–55% clay) in the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley; sandy loam from decomposed granite in Constantia (20–35% clay); lime-rich soils in Robertson
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Altitude and aspect
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge about 240–400 m; Elgin about 200–400 m; Cederberg about 1,030 m; Constantia favours cool east-, south-east- and south-facing slopes
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sea wind and distance
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Elim is about 15–17 km from the sea and its steady wind keeps yields low; Durbanville about 12 km; Hemel-en-Aarde about 5 km at the closest
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Rainfall
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Constantia about 1,000 mm, Elgin about 1,000 mm, Hemel-en-Aarde about 850 mm (750 mm in another source), Durbanville about 500–600 mm, Swartland about 200–500 mm
slides.1.content: In an answer, compare two regions side by side on soil, altitude, sea wind and rainfall; it scores better than describing one alone.
slides.2.title: Three contrasts
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Stellenbosch slope vs valley floor
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Slopes have free-draining decomposed granite and are cooler; valley floors have alluvial loam over clay subsoils that hold more water
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Swartland shale vs granite
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Malmesbury shale inland, granite on the Paardeberg and Kasteelberg, plus sandstone and quartzite higher up (such as Porseleinberg)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The three Hemel-en-Aarde wards
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Valley (80–200 m, Bokkeveld shale), Upper Valley (200–350 m, shale and decomposed granite), Ridge (240–400 m, shale with quartz seams); higher and more inland going up
slides.2.content: Changes in height and distance from the coast are the main driver of style differences between wards of one district.
